title: Manik Raitong's Flute (U Manik Raitong)
cultural_context: The legend of Manik Raitong, the orphaned bard who invented the Sharati flute and leaped into the funeral pyre playing his final lament.
lyrics_khasi:
Ha miet ba kynjah jar,
U Manik u kynud,
Ka sharati jong u
Ka pynsniew ki lyoh;
Sur pangnud ba shoh dohnud
Ka sawa ha ki them,
Ka Mahadei ka sngap
Na la ka ling-syiem.

Khlem khuslai ia ka jingiap,
U buh la ka sharati,
Ha thlen ka ding ba meh
U kiew khlem da shepteng;
U rwai haduh ba kut
Sur ba im ha la ka ri,
Ba pynsah nam u Manik
U nongrwai ba shisha.
lyrics_english:
In the deep silent night,
Manik softly piped,
His bamboo Sharati flute
Piercing through the mist;
A lament so heartbreaking
Echoing across valleys,
The Queen stood listening
From within the royal palace.

Without fear of impending death,
He held his sacred flute,
Onto the flaming pyre
He stepped without trembling;
Singing until the very end
A tune immortal in our land,
Preserving forever Manik's name,
The truest minstrel of our people.

khasi: Ha thlen ka ding ba meh
Sur ba im ha la ka ri,
english: A tune immortal in our land,
The truest minstrel of our people.

vocabulary.sharati: traditional bamboo flute of mourning and royalty
